n: Five documents from Friday through Sunday. The first is a post published Sunday on OpenAI's site. Its author proposes that AI developers compare their models on one shared measurement of how well a model predicts text, and agree on common limits they commit to not crossing. The second is from Anthropic's release notes, dated Friday. Computer use, where Claude can see a screen and work in the desktop apps a person allows, is now in beta on Team and Enterprise plans and is reaching organizations gradually. The third is from OpenAI's release notes, also Friday. A feature called Space is reaching Plus accounts for people 18 and older. It builds pages and presentations that can update from connected apps, and it does not offer public links. The fourth is a Friday post on Hugging Face about Inkling 2 Mini, an open model from Thinking Machines Lab that the post says is designed for local setups, meaning it runs on your own machine. The fifth is from OpenAI, Friday: a test of 99 chemistry problems drawn from 117 papers and patents. The top model earned 84.5 percent of the credit, and the page says the results do not establish whether models can discover new drugs. What it means for your work: every one of these documents states its own limit, in plain words, usually near the bottom. Who can use it, what it cannot share, what the score does not prove. Before you repeat a headline about an AI tool, find that sentence and read it first.
